Documentation → Administration → Upgrading to 3.0

Upgrading to SATOM 3.0

What 3.0 changes underneath the normal update — pack schema /2, one key per use, release notes only from signed packs, knowledge packs outside the update — and what online and air-gapped nodes must do, how to verify, and how to roll back.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → System → Software Update; shell: satom show trust, satom show knowledge, satom execute seed actions

In one paragraph#

SATOM 3.0 is applied like any update (Software update). What changes is where vendor knowledge comes from and which key may sign it: release notes, the Upgrade Advisory (called the Scout advisory at the time), upgrade paths, the API knowledge of builds you do not run, and signature metadata now arrive only in signed packs, in two lanes — the API pack pinned to each release and the rolling knowledge pack — each with its own key.

What breaks#

Change What it means for you
Pack schema satom.api-pack/2 3.0 packs carry a lane, a minimum SATOM version, the harvester snapshot and a kind on every item. SATOM 2.13 and older refuse them (unsupported pack schema). 3.0 still imports 2.x packs.
One key, one use Update packages: the update trust store, unchanged. Packs: only the key of their lane (api_pack or knowledge), shipped with the release. See Pack trust.
No vendor crawler SATOM no longer contacts any vendor documentation site; the Scan from Fortinet panel and its routes are gone. See Release notes.
Knowledge packs are not inside the update The release carries only its API pack (satom-apipack-3.0.0). The knowledge pack comes from the knowledge feed or by upload. See Knowledge packs.
New database objects The table for signature metadata and two columns of the API field-map table. Created by the update's migration.

Unchanged: the update packages and their key, the update procedure, the console URL, permissions, appliance credentials, and everything this node measured itself — local data always wins over any pack.

New in 3.0 as well: the read-only FortiGate workspace and the daily signature database freshness check.

What to do#

  1. 1Updateas usual, each node of a pair
  2. 2Seed the new actionssudo satom execute seed actions --yes, on the primary
  3. 3Knowledgeonline: automatic from the feed; air-gapped: upload the pack
  4. 4Verifysatom show trust · satom show knowledge

Online node or pair#

  1. Update (Software Update → Check / Apply, or an offline package). On a pair, update each node.
  2. Seed the two new scheduled actions once, on the primary. Scheduled actions are data, not code — no update creates them:

bash sudo satom execute seed actions # shows the plan sudo satom execute seed actions --yes # creates what is missing

This adds knowledge_fetch (daily) and signature_check (daily) if they are missing and never touches rows you edited. 3. Nothing else. The update imports the shipped API pack on the primary; from then on knowledge_fetch (default Download and import) brings each new knowledge pack. To pull one now: Knowledge packs → Check now → Import.

Nodes that reach an internal mirror and not the Internet: set the Feed URL on the Knowledge packs card of the primary.

Air-gapped node or pair#

  1. Update with the offline package and seed the actions as above. Set Scheduled fetch (daily) to Off or Notify if the feed can never be reached.
  2. Elsewhere, download the newest knowledge pack and its .sha256 from the knowledge release of the public SATOM repository; check it with sha256sum -c.
  3. On the primary, upload it under Software Update → API library packs and import it, or run sudo satom execute apipack import ./<pack> --yes.
  4. Repeat when you want newer knowledge: Release notes, the Upgrade Advisory and the Migration report show a stale badge after 30 days.

Container nodes#

The image carries the release's pack and the lane keys, but importing packs on a container install is not covered yet, and neither is the knowledge feed: treat the knowledge lanes as a known gap of 3.0.0 there.

How to verify#

satom show version      # 3.0.0 on every node
satom show trust        # three purposes: update, api_pack, knowledge
satom show knowledge    # installed pack per lane, age, mode, last fetch
satom show apipack      # packs and import history
Purpose Key Fingerprint
update satom-release-2026 SHA256:cYv9NxiJjMn/K6srKxXg2kdvROP2g6fzgfMXU6sxPyA
api_pack satom-apipack-2026 SHA256:tHXWO5UWTnvgoTloIzBpsN7J9Vj/NVbcTZFsdgww0ks
knowledge satom-knowledge-2026 SHA256:hVYALGlEVZISwsSFRvr6ymysCuYUo1NxecpUhLJXDjE

In the console: Software Update → Knowledge packs lists one row per lane without a stale badge; the Release Notes window reads Knowledge from <pack> (<date>); Administrator → Signatures shows a status per FortiWeb after the first signature_check run.

Rolling back#

A rollback to 2.13 is a normal downgrade (explicit confirmation on the page, --allow-downgrade on the console). A downgrade does not reverse database migrations (Offline updates):

  • The clean way back is the downgrade plus a restore of the database backup the 3.0 update took. Anything recorded after the update is lost with it.
  • Without the restore, the 3.0 table and columns stay. 2.13 ignores the signature-metadata table, but it does not know the field-map status column: rename candidates a 3.0 pack imported (never applied by 3.0) would read as ordinary field renames on 2.13. Retire them on API Field Renames before you downgrade, or restore the backup.
  • A 2.13 node refuses every 3.0 pack; the release notes already imported stay readable, but nothing newer arrives.
  • Keys you added under /etc/satom/pack-keys/ are ignored by 2.13.

Troubleshooting#

"unsupported pack schema" on a node#

The node still runs 2.13 or older. Update it to 3.0 first.

The Knowledge packs card stays empty after a day#

The scheduled action knowledge_fetch was never created: run sudo satom execute seed actions --yes on the primary, or press Check now and Import once.

"this api_pack pack is not signed by a trusted api_pack key …"#

The release tree on this node lacks its shipped pack keys (deploy/pack-keys/) or the file is not the official pack. Restore the release tree; see Pack trust.
